pins.title: Compression Boots for Nurses: Legs Heavy After a Long Shift? Start Here
pins.subtitle: Where do your legs feel heavy?
pins.description: The shift is over and your legs feel heavier than the rest of you. Before you buy compression boots, note where the heaviness sits for about three shifts. Feet up into thighs? Full-leg boots match that shape. Calves only? A calf device covers that with fewer parts. Mostly soles and ankles? None of these focuses there. Not medical advice. Read the full guide. #compressionboots #nurselife #nursesofinstagram #longshift #tiredlegs #legmassager

pins.title: Compression Boots vs Calf Sleeves: Full-Leg Boots or Calves Only?
pins.subtitle: Coverage vs setup
pins.description: Compression boots vs calf sleeves comes down to coverage and setup. The Normatec 3 Legs covers foot to upper thigh but needs a hose and control unit. The Normatec Go wraps the calves only, with no hose. The JetBoots Prime gives full-leg coverage, fully wireless. We compare zones, session times, sizing, and cleaning. Not medical advice. See the full comparison. #compressionboots #calfsleeves #normatec #jetboots #nurselife #legmassager

pins.title: Compression Boots for Nurses: 7-Point Checklist Before You Buy
pins.subtitle: Measure first, then choose
pins.description: Save this compression boots checklist. 1) Note where your legs feel heavy for about three shifts. 2) Measure before you choose a size. 3) Check your couch has room to stretch out. 4) Count the days you'd have 15 free minutes. 5) Accept that cleaning is limited. 6) Read the safety warnings. 7) Check who should skip them. Follow your manual wherever it differs. Not medical advice. Details in the guide. #compressionboots #nurselife #shiftworker #buyingguide #legmassager

pins.title: Compression Boots: Who Should Skip Them or Ask a Doctor First
pins.subtitle: Read the warnings first
pins.description: Thinking about compression boots after long shifts? Read the makers' warnings before you buy. Hyperice and Therabody list different conditions, including a history of blood clots, a pacemaker, and blood thinners. If one leg is painful, warm, or red, skip the device and see a doctor. You notice these signs in patients, so give your own legs the same look. Not medical advice. Read before you buy. #compressionboots #nurselife #nursehealth #longshift #legmassager
